system_summary.identity: Corvus is a governed developer-memory organ. Coding harnesses capture evidence, recall verified memories, and receive standing policy; a FastAPI service owns the private graph and trust gates; PostgreSQL holds canonical state; filesystem projections deliver capsules, skills, episode logs, and admission caches back to harnesses.
system_summary.primary_loop: session work -> redacted episode evidence -> frontier-grade distillation through the opus capability alias -> evidence frame -> near-duplicate check -> tiered write gate -> audited Action Bus mutation or human proposal -> cheap hybrid recall -> measured attribution -> janitor/auditor maintenance -> compiled skill and charter projection.
system_summary.governing_principle: Retrieval may fail open, but durable writes fail closed. Authoritative, identity-shaping, deduplication, reconsolidation, and reference-promotion decisions remain review-gated.

unchecked_invariants.statement: The distiller's attribution verdicts only nominate; no automatic outcome acts on them alone. Suppressed pathways keep a positive delivery floor (probe 1-in-k, never zero), zero-false-kills is computed from token-verified recurrence events rather than reward absence, and a tier-2 retirement proposal is refused unless it carries withheld-trial evidence with zero recurrences. Enforced executably by test_delivery_plasticity.py and test_recurrence_watch.py.

Horizontal recall uses PostgreSQL-canonical firing aggregates and bounded graph frontiers; its only retained graph-derived replica is revision-checked and history-bounded, and canonical startup mutations are serialized across workers.
Document-ingested reference facts enter at informational authority and can become lessons only through human-countersigned promotion.
A mapped mutation is allowed only after an admission pinned to the ledger's current revision; revision drift invalidates it.
Capture and ambient recall fail open for session continuity, but redact secrets and honor excluded cwd prefixes before disk or network use.
Agent tools are fail-closed against YAML allow-lists, every loop is turn/time bounded, and mutation claims are derived from Action rows.

memory_engine.title: Corvus-Mind memory engine
memory_engine.summary: The harness captures low-trust evidence outside the backend. The backend governs ingestion, executes provider-free hybrid recall, and runs bounded maintenance around PostgreSQL canonical state. Process-local matrices and filesystem projections are derivatives, never competing sources of truth.

zones.name: Agent and harness boundary
zones.purpose: Capture evidence and deliver memory without granting the coding agent direct graph authority.
details: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and Stop hooks drive delivery and capture.
PostToolUse and Stop append redacted episode JSONL under the local Corvus memory directory.
Thin MCP clients call backend HTTP endpoints; capture itself is not performed inside FastAPI.

Retrieved-lane hits pass a habituation pathway gate read from a filesystem projection — suppressed pathways deliver a deterministic 1-in-k probe and log everything else on the Injection record's `withheld` sibling list, keeping the hot path filesystem-only.

zones.name: Ingest and mutation governance
zones.purpose: Convert situated evidence into typed candidates and decide whether any durable mutation is authorized.
details: A systemd timer offers distillation every 30 minutes; only quiescent undistilled logs run, bounded to five sessions by default.
Distillation requests the opus capability grade, which resolves to Codex Sol by default and falls back to Anthropic Opus.
Evidence framing, near-duplicate routing, tiered write gates, reviewed proposals, and typed Action Bus handlers fail durable writes closed.

zones.name: Recall and evidence assembly
zones.purpose: Retrieve and assemble relevant evidence cheaply, observably, and without a provider LLM in the default hot path.
details: Embed-only neighbor voting classifies region and role; deterministic tokenization supplies keywords.
Embedding, PostgreSQL full-text, and named-entity lanes contribute candidates and are fused with reciprocal-rank fusion.
Six relevance-gated signals combine with a shrinking cold-start prior, region and role boosts, bounded graph spread, inhibition, and token-bounded assembly.

zones.name: Maintenance and projection
zones.purpose: Reopen weak or conflicting memory, preserve human judgment, and project trusted graph clusters back into harness capabilities.
details: Janitors prune firing history, decay utility, inspect staleness, classify delivery, and queue reviewable deduplication or reconsolidation work.
Pair and cross-scope judgment request the sonnet capability grade, which resolves to Codex Terra by default; canonical synthesis and the doubt auditor request the opus grade.
Deduplication and reconsolidation remain human-gated; successful graph changes refresh skills and standing-policy projections.

Delivery plasticity folds episode deliveries, withholdings, attribution verdicts, and verified recurrences into per-pathway habituation state; attenuation is a controlled trial of absence with a probe floor, and retirement is human-countersigned with causal trial evidence.

Synaptic downscaling renormalizes every neuron's homeostatic weight by a common factor on the distilled-session clock and lets a fixed floor do the selecting; it targets nothing by name, carries its own axis rather than the evidence scalar, and dormancy silences compiled delivery only, never direct recall.

zones.name: PostgreSQL canonical graph
zones.purpose: Own the durable tenant-scoped memory, topology, learning history, governance receipts, and provenance.
details: Neurons carry orthogonal node_type and abstraction_type semantics; parent_id and layer describe navigational projections rather than engine meaning.
Embeddings are 384-dimensional JSON arrays stored in TEXT columns; the deployed database does not use pgvector.
Stellate and pyramidal are conducting same-region and cross-region edges; evidence-link and supersedes edges carry memory semantics rather than activation.

zones.name: Revision-checked derived state
zones.purpose: Accelerate semantic selection without allowing a worker-local replica to become canonical.
details: Active neuron and engram embeddings load from PostgreSQL TEXT into a process-local NumPy float32 matrix.
PostgreSQL triggers advance a shared cache_versions revision when embeddings or the active set change.
Database coherence mode reads firing aggregates and bounded graph frontiers from PostgreSQL; the matrix reloads before semantic use when its revision is stale.

truth_notes.label: Embedding storage
truth_notes.value: PostgreSQL TEXT containing JSON vectors, searched through a revision-checked NumPy matrix; not pgvector.

truth_notes.label: Edge taxonomy
truth_notes.value: Stellate and pyramidal conduct activation; evidence-link and supersedes encode memory semantics.

truth_notes.label: Model routing
truth_notes.value: Workflows request capability grades; default aliases route opus→Codex Sol and sonnet→Codex Terra with same-grade Anthropic fallback.

truth_notes.label: Delivery habituation
truth_notes.value: Attenuation is a controlled trial of absence, not a verdict — the binomial tail nominates, exogenous evidence (probe rewards, token-verified recurrences of the suppressed lesson's failure) decides, and zero-false-kills is recurrence-grounded so the attribution proxy never grades itself.

truth_notes.label: Latency notation
truth_notes.value: Runtime latency belongs in live metrics with its observation window, not as a timeless constant in the static architecture.

decisions.title: Separate cheap recall from provider-model judgment
decisions.context: Recall is latency-sensitive and runs on every prompt/tool boundary; model-bearing judgment is slower, fallible, and provider-dependent.
decisions.decision: Default recall uses local embeddings, PostgreSQL, graph scoring, spread, inhibition, and assembly with no provider LLM; model calls are reserved for bounded workflows.
consequences: Ambient recall remains low-latency and available when provider CLIs fail.
Classification and retrieval quality must be improved through deterministic scoring rather than hidden inference.
alternatives: Invoke a model on every recall.
Use keyword-only retrieval with no semantic or graph stages.

decisions.title: Fail open for session continuity and fail closed for durable writes
decisions.context: Memory assistance must not strand a coding session, while a bad durable write compounds across every future session.
decisions.decision: Ambient recall/capture failures degrade without blocking the harness; durable mutations require evidence, typed validation, authority routing, and review where applicable.
consequences: Temporary memory outages reduce assistance rather than halting work.
Write paths carry more ceremony, audit state, and human review latency.
alternatives: Fail closed for every hook.
Permit best-effort direct graph writes from agents and model workflows.

decisions.title: Keep the operational frontend optional to the memory organ
decisions.context: Coding harnesses need memory continuously, while the human console is opened only for observation and judgment.
decisions.decision: Hooks, MCP, timers, API, and PostgreSQL operate independently of the React/Vite frontend; the UI remains a genuine but optional control plane.
consequences: Frontend failure does not disable recall or capture.
Every consequential UI action must have an explicit backend API contract.
alternatives: Couple memory operation to an open browser session.
Remove the human control plane and operate only through scripts.

decisions.title: Isolate tenants by database and process identity
decisions.context: Private developer memory and benchmark corpora must not share mutable graph state or lifecycle side effects.
decisions.decision: TENANT_ID fixes configuration and database identity for a process; corvus-mind and corvus-locomo use separate tenant configs and PostgreSQL databases.
consequences: Cross-tenant contamination is structurally harder.
Operations must verify tenant identity before running scripts, maintenance, or benchmarks.
alternatives: Shared tables with tenant_id on every row.
Separate repositories for each tenant.

decisions.title: Use one typed Action Bus for durable graph mutation
decisions.context: Proposals, agents, reconsolidation, maintenance, and explicit saves need consistent validation, audit, idempotency, and reversal semantics.
decisions.decision: Governed writers converge on typed Action Bus handlers and proposal application rather than creating workflow-specific mutation paths.
consequences: Mutation receipts are attributable and reusable across producers.
Direct model construction outside governed handlers becomes visible architectural debt.
alternatives: Allow each workflow to commit ORM changes directly.
Create separate mutation buses for proposals, agents, and janitors.

decisions.title: Project skills and standing capsules from canonical graph state
decisions.context: Harnesses need cheap pull-based playbooks and startup policy, but files can drift and lack graph-level provenance.
decisions.decision: Lessons remain canonical in PostgreSQL; compiler/projection services generate SKILL.md files, manifests, charter, and self-model capsules with source-neuron lineage.
consequences: Skills can be retracted or rebuilt when source lessons change.
Projection freshness and write-path isolation require explicit verification.
alternatives: Hand-author harness skills independently of memory.
Inject every lesson into every prompt.

decisions.title: Preserve forward intent in revisioned Roadmap Ledgers
decisions.context: Session memory preserves learned facts but is not a safe canonical store for unfinished plans, acceptance criteria, or strategic assumptions.
decisions.decision: Roadmap Ledgers are the canonical forward-intent register; mapped mutations require session admission pinned to the current ledger revision.
consequences: Agents receive durable kickoff context and cannot silently work against stale intent.
Off-ledger work must be explicit, and admissions never imply roadmap completion.
alternatives: Store plans only in transient agent plans or static markdown.
Infer permission from cwd without revision-aware admission.

decisions.title: Treat architecture as evidence-linked source-derived state
decisions.context: Hand-maintained diagrams decay as code, routes, deployments, and ownership boundaries change.
decisions.decision: The authored manifest explains intent; deterministic extraction reports source facts; conformance joins them, fingerprints freshness, and drives every Architecture UI view.
consequences: Contradictions and stale artifacts become visible rather than cosmetically corrected.
Static analysis limitations and accepted debt baselines must remain explicit.
alternatives: Maintain independent diagrams in a drawing tool.
Generate architecture solely from imports with no authored intent.

decisions.title: Do not hold database transactions across external model waits
decisions.context: Request-scoped AsyncSessions autobegin on graph reads and otherwise pin a bounded pooled connection while provider subprocesses can wait for minutes.
decisions.decision: Materialize DB inputs, explicitly commit/release the completed phase, run external model work in memory, then open a fresh persistence transaction.
consequences: Concurrent provider work no longer starves PostgreSQL connection capacity.
Query rows become visible only after model and pre-persistence citation work completes.
Boundary callers must ensure pending writes are semantically complete because the release commits them.
alternatives: Increase pool size while retaining request-long transactions.
Persist incomplete Query rows before provider execution.
Allocate a separate session for every individual stage.

decisions.title: Keep high-churn recall state PostgreSQL-canonical across workers
decisions.context: The firing index retained all historical query IDs per process, while adjacency and semantic caches were invalidated only inside the writer process; adding workers therefore multiplied memory and permitted divergent recall.
decisions.decision: Horizontal mode reads firing aggregates and bounded graph frontiers from PostgreSQL, retains only a bounded recent window in the optional single-worker index, and guards the small semantic matrix with a trigger-maintained shared revision.
consequences: Worker count no longer multiplies firing-history or adjacency memory, and committed graph changes are visible on the next canonical read.
Database-backed spread adds bounded SQL frontier reads; the semantic matrix adds one O(1) revision read per use.
Every database-backed spread records cap saturation and observed frontier/edge maxima in query telemetry; mind metrics aggregate cap-hit rate over the current recall window.
Process-local full adjacency/CSR remains an explicit single-worker latency mode, not a horizontal correctness mode.
PostgreSQL advisory locking serializes seed initialization across worker lifespans; schema mutation is an external Alembic deployment step.
alternatives: Broadcast local invalidations and reload the whole graph after nearly every query.
Move every embedding cosine operation into PostgreSQL without a vector index.
Accept sticky sessions and eventual cache divergence.

decisions.title: Make Alembic the sole schema-mutation authority
decisions.context: FastAPI lifespan mixed seeding with runtime DDL, the initial Alembic baseline could not bootstrap a blank database, deployment paths differed, and the live database had no alembic_version table.
decisions.decision: Docker and systemd share one migrate-then-start entry point; FastAPI independently requires the connected database heads to equal the packaged Alembic heads before any seed write.
consequences: Blank bootstrap, legacy upgrade, and normal deployment use one reviewed migration chain.
Unmanaged, behind, ahead, and unreachable schemas fail before application seeding.
Destructive migration tests accept only explicitly prefixed disposable database names.
Backup/restore verification preserves stable content checksums and extension/vector-index inventory parity.
alternatives: Continue application-owned idempotent DDL.
Stamp databases after out-of-band metadata.create_all.
Allow Docker, systemd, and direct Uvicorn starts to enforce different schema contracts.

decisions.title: Demote the attribution proxy to triage; trials of absence decide
decisions.context: Delivery plasticity wired distiller verdicts (which see only VISIBLE reliance) to an actuator — a survivor-bias ratchet tightened its own threshold, exculpatory evidence accrued at probe speed while condemnation ran full speed, and "zero false kills" was audited against the proxy's own rewards; prevention-style value is invisible in transcripts.
decisions.decision: The binomial tail only nominates. Attenuation is a controlled trial of absence with exogenous endpoints — probe rewards restore, and token-verified recurrences of a withheld lesson's documented failure restore plus book verified-false-kill receipts. Zero-false-kills is recurrence-grounded, tier-2 retirement requires causal trial evidence, and the contemplated base-rate drift monitor is deliberately not built.
consequences: A biased nomination wastes a cheap reversible trial instead of farming cobras; the ratchet becomes benign.
Withheld logging on Injection records is load-bearing infrastructure — without the denominator the trial is theater.
Nothing retires without observed withholding and zero recurrences; the human countersigns an experiment's result, not the distiller's opinion.
A missed recurrence is the safe direction — trial continues, exploration floor intact; vague legacy lessons simply enjoy stronger protection.
alternatives: Keep verdict-driven retirement and bolt on a base-rate drift monitor.
Give up on habituation and leave delivery-yield improvement human-driven.
Judge recurrences with a second model instead of a deterministic token gate.

processes.name: Start one tenant runtime
processes.trigger: Docker or systemd invokes the shared backend startup script; direct Uvicorn is reserved for an intentional schema-guard probe
processes.cadence: Once per process start
processes.why: Establish one tenant-isolated API process after the schema has been prepared explicitly by Alembic, then seed state, hot caches, action handlers, and remote MCP.
processes.outcome: FastAPI and /mcp serve against the TENANT_ID-derived database; the first hot recall avoids lazy cache cost.

steps.does: Set tenant/bind identity and run alembic upgrade head before executing Uvicorn.
steps.state_change: The selected tenant database reaches the migration head packaged with this build.
steps.guardrail: Migration or connectivity failure prevents Uvicorn from starting; Docker and systemd invoke the same script.

steps.does: Resolve the tenant's declared capability profile, then mount only that profile's routers and compose only its required startup steps.
steps.state_change: None; composition is decided before any router module of a disabled capability is imported.
steps.guardrail: A tenant with a missing, malformed, duplicated, or unrecognized capabilities block fails closed at startup with an actionable error rather than defaulting to mounting everything.

steps.does: Read the database's current Alembic heads and require exact equality with the packaged script heads.
steps.state_change: None; the check is read-only and runs before registries, seeds, or cache warmup.
steps.guardrail: Unmanaged, behind, ahead, and unreachable databases fail closed with an actionable migration error; the guard is declared unconditional so no capability profile can skip it.

steps.does: Load the action registry and seed core and engram data — each step only when a granted capability requires it.
steps.state_change: Bootstrap rows converge to the current code contract without implicit schema mutation; steps required by no granted capability never import their module.
steps.guardrail: Alembic is the explicit schema authority; no startup step contains a CREATE, ALTER, or metadata.create_all path.

steps.does: Load the local embedding model, semantic matrix, adjacency list, and CSR view when enabled.
steps.state_change: Process-local hot caches mirror active graph rows.
steps.guardrail: preload_on_startup is the explicit rollback switch.

steps.does: Enter the remote MCP session-manager lifespan and mount Streamable HTTP MCP at /mcp.
steps.state_change: Remote MCP sessions can be created for the running API worker.
steps.guardrail: Bare /mcp redirects with 307 so client methods are preserved.

processes.name: Open a coding session
processes.trigger: SessionStart hook
processes.cadence: Once per new or resumed harness session
processes.why: Put identity, standing policy, and roadmap obligations in the room before the first task while avoiding low-value subjectless recall.
processes.outcome: The harness receives self-model, charter, and roadmap admission context; no ambient graph recall runs at session open.

steps.does: Normalize the event and run memory injection plus roadmap context hooks.
steps.state_change: None in the backend; hook outputs are merged into additionalContext.
steps.guardrail: Hook exceptions exit zero so a memory outage cannot break the coding session.

steps.does: Read the designated mind-self-model and mind-charter projections from disk; SessionStart graph recall is intentionally disabled.
steps.state_change: Capsule source neurons are attribution-logged if newly delivered in the session.
steps.guardrail: Reference-class neurons cannot enter standing identity through the compiler eligibility filters.

steps.does: Resolve cwd against the local ledger cache, log admission-pending, and inject the current revision plus candidate records.
steps.state_change: PlanningAdmissionPending is appended to the episode timeline.
steps.guardrail: Cache absence is reported as unavailable, never interpreted as approval.

processes.name: Recall memory for a user prompt
processes.trigger: UserPromptSubmit with at least 15 characters
processes.cadence: Every substantive user prompt
processes.why: Deliver situated prior experience and relevant playbook pointers before the agent answers or acts.
processes.outcome: Up to six not-yet-seen one-line memory hooks and not-yet-shown skill pointers are injected and attributed.

steps.does: Derive the project from cwd and POST the prompt to /recall with source=hook_user_prompt.
steps.state_change: None locally until results return.
steps.guardrail: Excluded cwd prefixes bypass recall and logging; HTTP timeout is 2.5 seconds.

steps.does: Over-fetch candidates, run the canonical cheap pipeline, drop scaffold node types, apply project boost, and return real knowledge hits.
steps.state_change: When persist=true, a zero-cost Query row and firing rows record what was actually returned.
steps.guardrail: top_k is capped; scaffold nodes remain usable for graph spread but cannot consume delivered slots.

steps.does: Structural resolve, local embedding classification, hybrid lanes, six-signal score, continuity, spread, inhibition, optional engram resolve, token assembly, and telemetry.
steps.state_change: No graph mutation during preparation; process-local caches may load.
steps.guardrail: The canonical ordered stage list includes inhibition and contains no LLM classifier.

steps.does: Convert votes from source lessons and scored skill nodes into pull-based playbook pointers.
steps.state_change: Pointer delivery is logged for later conversion measurement.
steps.guardrail: A skill node is pointer fuel, never a delivered memory hit.

steps.does: Check each hit's (neuron, trigger, tool) pathway against the plasticity suppression projection; withhold suppressed pathways except the deterministic 1-in-k probe slot hashed from (session, pathway).
steps.state_change: Probe deliveries are stamped on the Injection record's `probes` list; suppressed hits land on its `withheld` sibling list — the denominator of the trial of absence, logged even when every hit was withheld.
steps.guardrail: A missing or corrupt projection fails open (deliver); no pathway state may reduce delivery probability to zero, and capsule standing content is never gated here.

steps.does: Dedupe against prior injections/pointers in the episode log and render summaries as background facts, not instructions.
steps.state_change: Injection and SkillPointer JSONL events link delivered neurons to the recall query id; withheld ids stay out of neuron_ids, dedupe, and attribution.
steps.guardrail: Full memory bodies are never ambiently injected; detail stays pull-based.

processes.name: Warn before a risky shell action
processes.trigger: PreToolUse for Bash commands with at least 15 characters
processes.cadence: Before qualifying shell calls
processes.why: Surface high-confidence machine and tool gotchas at the moment they can prevent a repeated failure.
processes.outcome: At most two unseen hits scoring at least 1.12 are injected; no skill pointers interrupt the tool call.

steps.does: Recall on the first 400 command characters with source=hook_pre_tool and project context, then apply the habituation pathway gate keyed per (neuron, PreToolUse, tool).
steps.state_change: Successful delivery is appended to the episode log; suppressed hits are logged withheld, probes stamped — same trial ledger as prompt delivery.
steps.guardrail: Non-Bash tools, short commands, low-score hits, and prior-session duplicates are ignored; the gate fails open.

steps.does: Run the same no-LLM graph path as prompt recall and return scored structured hits.
steps.state_change: Persist query/firing telemetry for later attribution.
steps.guardrail: Provider LLM modules are absent from the recall component.

processes.name: Admit a mapped project mutation
processes.trigger: PreToolUse detects a material operation targeting a mapped project
processes.cadence: Before the first mutation and again after any ledger revision change
processes.why: Keep coding work bound to canonical forward intent without turning memory retrieval into an enforcement mechanism.
processes.outcome: The mutation proceeds only with a current bound admission or an explicit off-ledger reason.

steps.does: Classify the tool and shell command as material/read-only, resolve target paths to the longest matching project ledger, and inspect the session episode.
steps.state_change: None on a permitted read; a denial is returned to the harness before the tool executes.
steps.guardrail: Multi-project mutations are blocked as ambiguous; unknown mutating tools fail toward admission.

steps.does: Validate unfinished record or off-ledger reason and append a PlanningAdmission event pinned to ledger revision/state version.
steps.state_change: Append-only admission receipt in the session episode log.
steps.guardrail: Done, cancelled, or deprioritized records cannot admit bound work.

steps.does: Re-read the latest admission; compare its revision to the local projection before allowing mutation.
steps.state_change: None.
steps.guardrail: Revision drift blocks and requires readmission.

processes.name: Capture session evidence
processes.trigger: PostToolUse and Stop hooks
processes.cadence: After each tool result and at session stop
processes.why: Preserve deeds and outcomes as low-trust evidence for later distillation without storing full file bodies or secrets.
processes.outcome: A per-session JSONL episode becomes distill-ready; planning return is recorded when admitted material work occurred.

steps.does: Summarize allow-listed tool inputs, derive structural success/failure, redact credential-shaped values, and append one event.
steps.state_change: ~/.corvus-mind/episodes/{session_id}.jsonl grows by one line.
steps.guardrail: Excluded cwd prefixes are never logged; arbitrary input fields are dropped; any exception exits zero.

steps.does: On Stop, inspect post-admission successful material tool events and append PlanningReturn with reconcile-required status.
steps.state_change: Execution evidence is returned to the episode timeline; canonical roadmap status does not auto-close.
steps.guardrail: No admission or no material work produces no return receipt.

processes.name: Explicitly recall institutional memory
processes.trigger: Agent calls the corvus-mind recall MCP tool
processes.cadence: On demand
processes.why: Pull full evidence-framed memory when ambient one-line hooks are insufficient.
processes.outcome: Structured hits with content, provenance, timestamps, scores, query id, telemetry, and skill pointers.

steps.does: POST /recall with include_content=true and source=mcp; it imports no application or database modules.
steps.state_change: None in the client.
steps.guardrail: Backend errors are returned as tool JSON instead of crashing the MCP process.

steps.does: Execute cheap hybrid retrieval; in horizontal mode read firing aggregates and bounded spread frontiers from PostgreSQL, checking the shared semantic revision before cosine selection.
steps.state_change: Query/firing telemetry persists by default; committed graph writes become visible to every worker on its next canonical read or semantic revision check.
steps.guardrail: Memory-surface dependency 404s the endpoint on non-memory tenants; database spread caps frontier nodes and returned edges per hop.

processes.name: Save one explicit lesson
processes.trigger: Agent calls remember with claim, evidence, future use, and likely queries
processes.cadence: On demand after verified learning
processes.why: Preserve situated knowledge in a form a future agent can reconstruct without this transcript.
processes.outcome: A novel low-authority lesson is audited and embedded, or a near-duplicate/authoritative write remains queued for review.

steps.does: Send the nine evidence-frame slots to /remember at informational authority.
steps.state_change: None in the client.
steps.guardrail: future_use and likely_queries are required tool arguments.

steps.does: Resolve a scope/project anchor, normalize entities, build the canonical evidence frame, and stage a proposal item.
steps.state_change: Proposal and proposal-item rows describe the candidate before any neuron exists.
steps.guardrail: Missing/malformed frame slots fail with 422; no caller gets an unframed durable memory.

steps.does: Compare nearest active lessons, queue ambiguous duplicates, then classify the proposal by authority, guardrail result, confidence, and region override.
steps.state_change: Proposal stays proposed or becomes approved/applied by the system gate.
steps.guardrail: The memory tenant requires approval for dedup; writes above guidance cannot auto-commit.

steps.does: Apply the approved proposal through typed, validated, audited handlers inside a savepoint.
steps.state_change: Neuron/refinement/action rows change atomically within the outer transaction.
steps.guardrail: Handler failure rolls back its savepoint and records a failed Action rather than a partial success.

steps.does: Embed a newly created neuron, wire nearest-neighbor edges, and update the writer's optional local projections before commit returns.
steps.state_change: PostgreSQL becomes canonical at commit; embedding/active-set triggers advance the shared semantic revision so every worker reloads before its next semantic use.
steps.guardrail: Cache/index update occurs only after a real created neuron id exists; local updates are optimizations, not cross-worker coherence.

processes.name: Distill episodes into candidate lessons
processes.trigger: corvus-mind-distill.timer POSTs /distill/run
processes.cadence: Timer opportunity every 30 minutes; only quiescent undistilled logs run, max five sessions by default
processes.why: Convert noisy tool evidence and user corrections into durable, future-useful lessons while preventing self-reinforcement and agent-assertion pollution.
processes.outcome: Gate-passed candidates traverse the same lesson write path; attribution rewards/penalizes previously injected memories; recurrence nominations for withheld lessons pass a deterministic admission gate; successful logs receive markers.

steps.does: Offer a bounded POST to /distill/run.
steps.state_change: Starts one batch request.
steps.guardrail: Service timeout and per-run session cap bound work.

steps.does: Load redacted events, injections, user messages, and lowest-trust assistant assertions; request the opus capability grade for framed candidates and attribution verdicts (Codex Sol primary by default, Anthropic Opus fallback).
steps.state_change: Provider usage is recorded; no candidate is saved yet.
steps.guardrail: Assistant-origin candidates require a cited corroborating tool event; instruction-shaped and already-injected lessons are dropped.

steps.does: Route each surviving candidate through proposal, near-duplicate, authority, and Action Bus controls.
steps.state_change: Candidate becomes a neuron or remains a review proposal.
steps.guardrail: One bad candidate is counted and skipped without aborting the session batch.

steps.does: Reward load-bearing injections, demote contradicted ones, leave unused unchanged, and attach SynapticLearningEvent when query-linked.
steps.state_change: avg_utility and attribution telemetry move from observed session outcomes.
steps.guardrail: One verdict per label per session; ambiguous delivery channel is labeled rather than guessed.

steps.does: Present lessons a delivery trial withheld from this session and ask whether each one's documented failure actually recurred in the log.
steps.state_change: None — nominations are model output, not decisions; refused ones are counted and dropped.
steps.guardrail: Only lessons never delivered anywhere in the session qualify; delivered-and-failed is contradiction evidence for the attribution lane, not trial harm.

steps.does: Admit a nomination only when its cited event token-matches both the actual episode events and the withheld lesson's own failure text, then log recurrence.verified per withheld pathway.
steps.state_change: Ground-truth false-kill evidence lands in the actions log for the plasticity fold to consume.
steps.guardrail: Uncited or unrelated nominations are refused (deeds-corroborated pattern); a missed match leaves the trial running with the pathway's floor intact — the safe failure direction.

steps.does: Commit and write a .distilled marker only after the session completes successfully.
steps.state_change: The log leaves the ready queue; failures without markers retry later.
steps.guardrail: Per-log failure does not stop other ready logs.

processes.name: Compile lessons into playbooks and standing policy
processes.trigger: corvus-mind-compile.timer POSTs /compile/run
processes.cadence: Daily opportunity; bounded new skills per run
processes.why: Convert related trusted memories into reusable procedures while keeping graph truth, projections, and harness delivery synchronized.
processes.outcome: Stale projections retire to archive; eligible clusters produce mind-* skills and graph-shadow nodes; charter is deterministically rebuilt.

steps.does: Load eligible lessons, build same-scope embedding components, split oversized clusters, and reconcile manifest entries against disk/source health.
steps.state_change: None until stale or new artifacts are identified.
steps.guardrail: Source utility, active/superseded state, cluster growth, size caps, and namespacing constrain eligibility.

steps.does: Request the opus capability grade to compose one focused name, description, and Markdown playbook from each new eligible cluster; default routing selects Codex Sol with Anthropic Opus fallback.
steps.state_change: Model usage is added to the compile report.
steps.guardrail: Invalid JSON, non-mind-* names, or missing fields emit no skill.

steps.does: Write generated SKILL.md with source-neuron provenance and project it to supported harnesses.
steps.state_change: Canonical and harness skill files plus compiled-skills manifest change.
steps.guardrail: Only namespaced generated directories are written; retired renderings are archived, not deleted.

steps.does: Create an informational skill-shadow neuron and evidence-link edges from its source lessons.
steps.state_change: The graph can score the skill as pointer fuel and visualize its source cluster.
steps.guardrail: Recall filters skill nodes from memory hits.

steps.does: Deterministically render only guidance/organizational, standing-delivery, non-reference lessons within a character cap.
steps.state_change: mind-charter projection and manifest entry refresh.
steps.guardrail: An unclassified corpus cannot blank an existing charter; overflow is logged.

processes.name: Run bounded memory janitors
processes.trigger: corvus-mind-janitor.timer POSTs /janitor/run
processes.cadence: Timer opportunity every 6 hours; decay and similar cadence-sensitive work use distilled-session evidence time
processes.why: Prevent duplicate mass, stale facts, warm zombies, scope drift, stale approvals, and standing-policy drift from accumulating.
processes.outcome: Safe low-risk metadata changes apply; destructive/synthesis/reference promotion decisions become proposals; delivery pathways habituate/restore with zero-false-kill accounting; reports and change logs remain auditable.

steps.does: Run selected consolidation, staleness, decay, charter promotion, reference promotion, delivery classification, scope lint, and stale-approved passes.
steps.state_change: Each pass returns a bounded report and persists change events/actions.
steps.guardrail: Per-pass limits bound mutations and critic volume.

steps.does: Detect similar lesson components, request sonnet-grade pair and cross-scope verdicts (Codex Terra primary by default), and request opus-grade FusionPlan synthesis when rewiring is warranted.
steps.state_change: Review proposals are queued; silent fusion is disabled on the mind tenant.
steps.guardrail: Human approval is required for dedup/reconsolidation and stale plans revalidate against live member state.

steps.does: Supersede perishable older facts when evidence supports a newer one and demote frequently recalled never-reinforced memories.
steps.state_change: is_active, superseded_by, avg_utility, edges, findings, and temporal change log may update.
steps.guardrail: Stable identity facts and organizational standing conflicts are protected; decay runs on new distilled sessions, not wall clock alone.

steps.does: Adjust earned authority, queue reference graduation, and classify whether trusted lessons belong in standing or retrieved delivery.
steps.state_change: authority/delivery metadata or review proposals change.
steps.guardrail: Organizational authority is human-set; reference facts cannot auto-enter charter identity.

steps.does: Run last so it folds this cycle's attribution — episode deliveries, withholdings, verdicts, and verified recurrences become per-pathway counters; attenuate statistically dead pathways in rewarding channels, restore on probe rewards or recurrences (booking verified-false-kill incident receipts), and queue tier-2 retirement proposals carrying the trial as a causal claim.
steps.state_change: delivery_pathways states, the hot-path suppression projection, and false-kill receipts in the actions log update; the neuron itself is never touched.
steps.guardrail: Sole writer; binomial tail is triage only; young pathways are immune; no state reaches zero delivery probability; retirement requires an applied human countersign and trial_claim refuses proposals without withheld-trial evidence.

steps.does: Retract skills citing retired sources, deactivate graph shadows, and rebuild the charter when required.
steps.state_change: Disk projections and manifest no longer cite retired neuron ids.
steps.guardrail: Projection refresh runs post-commit so files cannot move ahead of a rolled-back graph transaction.

processes.name: Run a delivery-pathway trial of absence
processes.trigger: The plasticity fold attenuates a (neuron, trigger, tool) pathway whose deliveries earn no rewards in a channel that rewards others
processes.cadence: Continuous once attenuated; one trial spans hook deliveries, distill cycles, and janitor passes until it resolves
processes.why: Attribution verdicts only see VISIBLE reliance, so unrewarded is not the same as useless — a prevented mistake leaves no transcript trace. Withholding is the only mechanism that can make prevention-value visible; the proxy nominates, the trial decides (mind-delivery-plasticity + mind-recurrence-watch).
processes.outcome: The pathway either earns restoration — a probe reward, or a verified recurrence of its lesson's documented failure that also books a first-class false-kill incident receipt — or accumulates clean trial evidence toward a human-countersigned retirement that still keeps a probe floor.

steps.does: Attenuate when P(0 rewards in n deliveries | channel base reward rate) falls below alpha, with n counted since the last exculpation and immunity for young pathways; project suppression state to the file the hook reads.
steps.state_change: Pathway state and the suppression projection change; the neuron itself keeps full graph standing and MCP recallability.
steps.guardrail: The binomial tail is triage, never a verdict — a channel that rewards nobody can never condemn (dead and starved must not look alike), and every transition is audit-logged.

steps.does: Withhold the suppressed pathway from most sessions and deliver a deterministic 1-in-k probe on the rest, logging both outcomes on the Injection record.
steps.state_change: The `withheld` sibling list accumulates the trial's denominator; `probes` marks deliveries that can earn dishabituation.
steps.guardrail: Fail open on missing projection; withheld ids never enter neuron_ids, session dedupe, or attribution; a trial without logged withholding is not evidence.

steps.does: On each distill of a session that withheld the lesson, look for its documented failure mode actually recurring in the tool events.
steps.state_change: Nominations only — the model proposes, it never decides.
steps.guardrail: Lessons delivered anywhere in the session are excluded; delivered-and-failed routes to the contradiction lane instead.

steps.does: Token-verify each nomination against the episode log AND the lesson's own failure text; on admission the next fold restores the pathway, books a plasticity.false_kill receipt, anchors the exculpation clock so the restore is not undone, and supersedes any pending retirement proposal.
steps.state_change: Verified false kills surface first-class in the janitor report and the delivery-pathways metrics — computed from recurrence events, never reward absence.
steps.guardrail: The proxy that nominates never grades its own outcomes; a missed recurrence is the safe direction (trial continues, floor intact). The base-rate drift monitor was deliberately not built — triage-only nomination makes that ratchet benign.

steps.does: Review a retirement proposal whose body is a causal claim — sessions withheld with window, probes fired and their outcomes, recurrence count zero — rather than a verdict-shaped statistical argument.
steps.state_change: Only an APPLIED proposal lets the sole writer retire the pathway; even retired keeps a small probe floor and reopens on new evidence.
steps.guardrail: Proposals without trial evidence are refused before staging; a rejected proposal blocks re-proposal; a recurrence during retire-proposed supersedes it.

processes.name: Reopen risky memories
processes.trigger: 12-hour timer opportunity in auto mode, explicit light/deep run, or event audit of one neuron
processes.cadence: Evidence clock selects skip/light/deep from fresh distilled sessions
processes.why: Find subtle defects deterministic janitors cannot see and turn uncertainty into reviewable proposals without granting a critic write power.
processes.outcome: Ranked risk packets receive bounded opus-grade critiques through provider aliases; valid verdicts may open quality proposals; watermark and precision/volume evidence are logged.

steps.does: Score active lessons from conflict, duplicate, age, utility, provenance, and prior-decision signals; add rotated deep probes and healthy controls.
steps.state_change: None during scoring.
steps.guardrail: Candidate, control, probe, and critic counts are hard-capped.

steps.does: Judge evidence packets with prior decisions and source context, then validate the verdict against packet facts.
steps.state_change: Provider usage and auditor ledger entries record the review.
steps.guardrail: Invalid or unsupported verdicts are rejected; critic concurrency is capped at two for machine memory safety.

steps.does: Queue bounded quality proposals for human review instead of editing the neuron.
steps.state_change: Proposal rows and evidence packets enter the inbox.
steps.guardrail: Duplicate open hits and heightened-review classes remain gated.

processes.name: Ingest a book into reference memory
processes.trigger: Operator uploads a supported file to /admin/reference/documents
processes.cadence: On demand
processes.why: Add sourced reference knowledge without confusing a document's claims with lived, verified agent experience.
processes.outcome: Informational Library facts are embedded, linked to a SourceDocument, discounted at cold start, and revocable as a document set.

steps.does: Validate size/format, parse text/structure, ensure Library region, supersede prior canonical version, create job, and start a background task.
steps.state_change: SourceDocument and DocumentIngestJob rows persist before extraction begins.
steps.guardrail: Authority is fixed at informational; re-ingest revokes the prior active version.

steps.does: Choose whole-document or section-aware chunks, request the opus capability grade for self-contained faithful facts, and bound total facts.
steps.state_change: Job progress and provider usage update as chunks complete.
steps.guardrail: Prompt treats document instructions as data; empty/invalid facts are discarded.

steps.does: Stage each fact as an informational proposal and apply through the same write gate and Action Bus as organic lessons.
steps.state_change: Reference neurons and Action audit rows are created.
steps.guardrail: Library region overrides cap authority and discount cold-start prior.

steps.does: Link created neurons to SourceDocument and document anchor, then embed and KNN-wire them.
steps.state_change: NeuronSourceLink, graph edges, and hot indexes update.
steps.guardrail: A fact is reported saved only with its provenance link.

steps.does: Deactivate every still-reference neuron linked to the document, preserve links/change events, retain human-promoted graduates, and invalidate caches.
steps.state_change: Document status and active neuron set change immediately.
steps.guardrail: Nothing is deleted; promoted lessons are reported for separate judgment.

processes.name: Extract and place knowledge-tenant documents
processes.trigger: Operator uploads through /admin/documents/upload
processes.cadence: On demand; hidden from the corvus-mind memory-surface navigation
processes.why: Preserve the two-phase document pipeline still used by knowledge-graph deployments and historical Corvus surfaces.
processes.outcome: Frontier-grade extraction artifacts are placed one-by-one by the neuron_placer agent, then enter the normal human proposal queue.

steps.does: Parse synchronously, persist a job, and start background Phase 1 extraction.
steps.state_change: DocumentIngestJob enters analyzing state.
steps.guardrail: File size/format and cancellation are enforced.

steps.does: Read the whole document when it fits, otherwise process sections, and create content-only artifact proposals without placement fields.
steps.state_change: Proposal rows enter artifact state with section/page evidence.
steps.guardrail: Placement is explicitly out of Phase 1; extraction output is parsed and retried under bounds.

steps.does: Read one artifact, search legal parents, commit placement or uncertainty, and perform mandatory read-back verification.
steps.state_change: Artifact becomes proposed with placement, or remains artifact/uncertain with candidate homes.
steps.guardrail: One artifact per run; content immutable; mutation plus verification required before done.

steps.does: Review placed proposals before any neuron is created.
steps.state_change: Approved proposals can proceed to Action Bus application.
steps.guardrail: The placement agent has no direct neuron-creation tool.

processes.name: Review and apply a proposed graph change
processes.trigger: Human acts in Inbox/Proposal Queue or calls proposal APIs
processes.cadence: On demand
processes.why: Separate machine-produced judgment from authority to change durable graph state.
processes.outcome: Proposal is rejected, approved awaiting application, or applied with typed Action evidence and post-apply cache/projection refresh.

steps.does: Present producer origin, items, provenance, dedup/FusionPlan preview, and review controls.
steps.state_change: None until the reviewer acts.
steps.guardrail: Identity/role checks determine review and apply permissions.

steps.does: Lock the proposal, record approve/reject decision, reviewer, notes, and timestamp.
steps.state_change: Proposal state becomes approved or rejected.
steps.guardrail: Only proposed rows are reviewable; self/role policies are enforced by RBAC.

steps.does: Revalidate approved proposal and submit the proposal.apply action tree.
steps.state_change: Child neuron create/refine/reconsolidate actions execute and audit rows link to the proposal.
steps.guardrail: Stale FusionPlans fail closed against live member fingerprints.

steps.does: Resolve originating findings, refresh graph indexes, and trigger reconsolidation-dependent cleanup.
steps.state_change: Findings and cache/projection state converge with the applied graph.
steps.guardrail: Cleanup runs only after an applied proposal.

processes.name: Run a graph-grounded answer
processes.trigger: POST /query, /query/stream, /v1/query, or the legacy Corvus MCP query_graph tool
processes.cadence: On demand; Query Lab is hidden on the current memory-surface nav but the APIs remain live
processes.why: Produce and compare model answers grounded in graph context with deterministic citation and output controls.
processes.outcome: Query, slots, telemetry, costs, firings, citation audit, and response are persisted; streaming callers see each stage.

steps.does: Validate request, run deterministic input guard, normalize model slots, and invoke execute_query.
steps.state_change: None before the executor creates a Query row.
steps.guardrail: Blocked input returns 403; stage failures name the failed stage.

steps.does: Run ordered cheap prep; reuse persisted-session context only when fresh-pack overlap crosses the drift gate.
steps.state_change: No durable write; the actual primary prompt and slot contract are held in a transient Query object.
steps.guardrail: Raw comparison slots receive no neuron context; A/B slots are not silently tier-swapped.

steps.does: Commit the completed graph-read phase and return its pooled PostgreSQL connection before any answer, citation-repair, or judge model can wait.
steps.state_change: The read transaction ends; loaded context remains in memory and no Query row is durable yet.
steps.guardrail: Provider-slot helpers receive no AsyncSession; the next database operation starts a fresh persistence transaction.

steps.does: Execute one or more neuron/raw slots concurrently, apply primary effort/model floors and optional tier escalation, and preserve per-slot usage.
steps.state_change: Slot results accumulate in memory before final persistence.
steps.guardrail: Provider alias fallback is explicit; persisted-session state applies only to primary slot; no database handle enters the slot.

steps.does: Verify per-query random citation keys, strip/repair fabricated keys, score claim/source relevance, escalate the ambiguous band to entailment, and run tenant output policies.
steps.state_change: Pre-persistence citation artifacts accumulate in memory; CitationHopSession and OutputViolation rows persist only after provider work.
steps.guardrail: Valid-key existence and claim support are separate layers; relevance failure is advisory.

steps.does: Persist primary response, costs/results, regulatory coverage gaps, counters, neuron/engram firings, and co-fire learning.
steps.state_change: Query/telemetry/graph usage history becomes evaluation and learning input.
steps.guardrail: Only actually included sources receive included-position credit.

steps.does: Emit bounded SSE stage, result, and error events while the same executor runs in a task.
steps.state_change: Same as non-streaming path.
steps.guardrail: Queue is bounded and cancelled if the consumer exits.

processes.name: Run a maintenance agent
processes.trigger: Admin POSTs /v1/agents/{name}/run or a workflow invokes execute_agent
processes.cadence: On demand; all YAML schedules are currently disabled
processes.why: Delegate narrow judgment to a model while retaining deterministic tool, mutation, verification, and audit boundaries.
processes.outcome: A root agent.run Action and child tool Actions provide the authoritative record; proposals or placements may change, never by unrecorded prose.

steps.does: Load YAML definitions and validate every allowed tool against the ToolRegistry.
steps.state_change: Process-local immutable agent definitions become available.
steps.guardrail: Unknown YAML keys or tools fail closed at load time.

steps.does: Create root Action, call the configured provider, parse one JSON envelope per turn, and dispatch only allowed tools.
steps.state_change: Root/child Action rows and tool effects persist.
steps.guardrail: max_turns hard cap 20, tool timeout 60 seconds, schema validation, allow-list, and bounded done-rejections.

steps.does: Commit each successful mutating tool immediately and derive final summary from the Action trail rather than the model's self-report.
steps.state_change: Mutations survive later-turn failure and claims remain auditable.
steps.guardrail: Profiles can require expected mutation count and a post-mutation verification tool before done.

processes.name: Maintain forward intent and reconcile execution
processes.trigger: Operator creates/edits/reviews a ledger or a harness requests admission context
processes.cadence: On planning change and after execution evidence is independently accepted
processes.why: Keep plans, prerequisites, assumptions, reviews, and verified outcomes durable without confusing retrospective memory with future intent.
processes.outcome: Canonical JSON state advances under optimistic concurrency; a compact atomic projection feeds hooks; accepted evidence can close records.

steps.does: Edit sections, records, edges, milestones, assumptions, horizons, cadence, prompts, and verification criteria.
steps.state_change: A full candidate state is sent with expected_revision.
steps.guardrail: UI does not bypass backend validation or revision checks.

steps.does: Validate IDs/statuses/prerequisites/reviews/assumptions, lock the row, reject stale revisions, advance state version, and commit.
steps.state_change: roadmap_ledgers.state and revision increment atomically.
steps.guardrail: Unknown references, invalid status/horizon/cadence, and stale expected_revision fail.

steps.does: Rank a small candidate shortlist and atomically replace owner-only ~/.corvus-mind/planning/ledgers.json.
steps.state_change: Hooks see the new revision without reading PostgreSQL.
steps.guardrail: Cache failure never rolls back canonical ledger state.

steps.does: Attach reconciliation claims, limitations, disclosures, evidence, verifier, and accepting human; close only verified complete work.
steps.state_change: Record receipt/history update and ledger revision increment.
steps.guardrail: Verifier cannot equal accepting human; verified completion requires checklist and evidence.

processes.name: Observe system behavior
processes.trigger: Operator opens Pallium, Sessions, Skills, Performance, Eval, Labs, or Architecture
processes.cadence: On demand
processes.why: Make trust, retrieval, maintenance, cost, latency, skill conversion, benchmark, and structural drift inspectable without changing graph truth.
processes.outcome: Read models combine PostgreSQL aggregates, episode/manifest/eval artifacts, provider usage probes, and generated source maps.

steps.does: Fetch a purpose-specific read endpoint through the Vite proxy and render desktop/mobile shell-agnostic views.
steps.state_change: Browser state only.
steps.guardrail: Demo builds substitute captured fixtures; normal builds call live endpoints.

steps.does: Aggregate database rows and local artifacts into trust, channel, sessions, skills, cost, stage latency, immutable run, and experiment reports.
steps.state_change: Most reads are side-effect free; subscription probes may refresh process-local/cache data only.
steps.guardrail: Missing optional artifacts return explicit absent/empty states.

steps.does: Serve committed extraction/conformance artifacts rather than walking the repository on each page load.
steps.state_change: None.
steps.guardrail: Missing or invalid artifacts return explicit 404/500 detail.

processes.name: Run the isolated LoCoMo lifecycle benchmark
processes.trigger: Explicit eval/locomo harness command
processes.cadence: On demand for a frozen benchmark or experimental arm
processes.why: Measure behavior under a known corpus without contaminating the production mind graph.
processes.outcome: Ingest, answer, maintenance, judge, refusal, and token artifacts are archived under timestamped eval directories and summarized in Observe.

steps.does: Select TENANT_ID=corvus-locomo and separate database, reset/seed as required, and run ingest/answer/nospread/baseline/lifecycle phases.
steps.state_change: Only the benchmark database and eval artifact tree change.
steps.guardrail: Production corvus_mind rows are not reused.

steps.does: Run production retrieval, scoring, spread, inhibition, and assembly settings for the selected arm.
steps.state_change: Benchmark Query/firing rows record the arm.
steps.guardrail: Arm configuration and corpus receipt are archived.

steps.does: Invoke production janitor/auditor behavior where the benchmark protocol requires maintenance.
steps.state_change: Benchmark graph evolves through the same gated lifecycle.
steps.guardrail: Artifacts record before/after corpus state and errors.

steps.does: Score every question, enforce adversarial refusal policy, aggregate categories, and publish latest Oracle Funnel/Locomo status.
steps.state_change: Immutable result JSON and summary artifacts accumulate.
steps.guardrail: Complete-run certificates require expected question counts.

processes.name: Refresh the architecture atlas
processes.trigger: Code changes or an explicit architecture review
processes.cadence: Before claiming this page describes the current source
processes.why: Keep the explanatory model falsifiable against code instead of allowing a hand-drawn diagram to age silently.
processes.outcome: architecture.json, conformance.json, coverage, drift, routes, runtime, components, and process evidence all reflect one source state.

steps.does: Walk every Python module; derive imports, calls, HTTP/MCP routes, DB-write/LLM sites, cycles, and background candidates.
steps.state_change: architecture/architecture.json is replaced.
steps.guardrail: Stdlib-only deterministic analysis; parse errors are counted.

steps.does: Walk TypeScript, resolve direct/API-wrapper URLs, and join normalized frontend callers to backend full paths.
steps.state_change: Frontend inventory and route join are embedded in architecture.json.
steps.guardrail: Unresolvable URLs are reported rather than guessed.

steps.does: Classify every source unit, check invariants, verify runtime/process evidence, and report unclassified or contradicted claims.
steps.state_change: architecture/conformance.json is replaced.
steps.guardrail: Authored explanation and derived facts remain separate artifacts.

processes.name: Publish the static public demo
processes.trigger: Operator runs npm run demo:publish and pushes the exact reviewed state to the demo branch
processes.cadence: Explicit release only
processes.why: Demonstrate the interface without exposing private source data, a database, backend endpoints, or provider credentials.
processes.outcome: Render serves a noindex fixture-backed static bundle; rollback is a prior Render deployment.

steps.does: Capture approved live endpoint fixtures, validate their contracts, and build with VITE_DEMO=1.
steps.state_change: Reviewed frontend fixture JSON and static dist change locally.
steps.guardrail: Publish fails on fixture contract drift; fixtures ship verbatim and require review.

steps.does: Exercise the demo bundle before branch publication.
steps.state_change: Test artifacts only.
steps.guardrail: A failing browser test stops the publish script.

steps.does: Build the frontend subdirectory from the demo branch and serve dist with SPA fallback.
steps.state_change: Public static deployment updates.
steps.guardrail: The Python backend is absent; X-Robots-Tag is noindex,nofollow.

paths.name: Start one tenant runtime
paths.trigger: Docker or systemd invokes the shared backend startup script; direct Uvicorn is reserved for an intentional schema-guard probe
paths.cadence: Once per process start
paths.why: Establish one tenant-isolated API process after the schema has been prepared explicitly by Alembic, then seed state, hot caches, action handlers, and remote MCP.
paths.outcome: FastAPI and /mcp serve against the TENANT_ID-derived database; the first hot recall avoids lazy cache cost.

steps.does: Set tenant/bind identity and run alembic upgrade head before executing Uvicorn.
steps.state_change: The selected tenant database reaches the migration head packaged with this build.
steps.guardrail: Migration or connectivity failure prevents Uvicorn from starting; Docker and systemd invoke the same script.

steps.does: Resolve the tenant's declared capability profile, then mount only that profile's routers and compose only its required startup steps.
steps.state_change: None; composition is decided before any router module of a disabled capability is imported.
steps.guardrail: A tenant with a missing, malformed, duplicated, or unrecognized capabilities block fails closed at startup with an actionable error rather than defaulting to mounting everything.

steps.does: Read the database's current Alembic heads and require exact equality with the packaged script heads.
steps.state_change: None; the check is read-only and runs before registries, seeds, or cache warmup.
steps.guardrail: Unmanaged, behind, ahead, and unreachable databases fail closed with an actionable migration error; the guard is declared unconditional so no capability profile can skip it.

steps.does: Load the action registry and seed core and engram data — each step only when a granted capability requires it.
steps.state_change: Bootstrap rows converge to the current code contract without implicit schema mutation; steps required by no granted capability never import their module.
steps.guardrail: Alembic is the explicit schema authority; no startup step contains a CREATE, ALTER, or metadata.create_all path.

steps.does: Load the local embedding model, semantic matrix, adjacency list, and CSR view when enabled.
steps.state_change: Process-local hot caches mirror active graph rows.
steps.guardrail: preload_on_startup is the explicit rollback switch.

steps.does: Enter the remote MCP session-manager lifespan and mount Streamable HTTP MCP at /mcp.
steps.state_change: Remote MCP sessions can be created for the running API worker.
steps.guardrail: Bare /mcp redirects with 307 so client methods are preserved.

paths.name: Open a coding session
paths.trigger: SessionStart hook
paths.cadence: Once per new or resumed harness session
paths.why: Put identity, standing policy, and roadmap obligations in the room before the first task while avoiding low-value subjectless recall.
paths.outcome: The harness receives self-model, charter, and roadmap admission context; no ambient graph recall runs at session open.

steps.does: Normalize the event and run memory injection plus roadmap context hooks.
steps.state_change: None in the backend; hook outputs are merged into additionalContext.
steps.guardrail: Hook exceptions exit zero so a memory outage cannot break the coding session.

steps.does: Read the designated mind-self-model and mind-charter projections from disk; SessionStart graph recall is intentionally disabled.
steps.state_change: Capsule source neurons are attribution-logged if newly delivered in the session.
steps.guardrail: Reference-class neurons cannot enter standing identity through the compiler eligibility filters.

steps.does: Resolve cwd against the local ledger cache, log admission-pending, and inject the current revision plus candidate records.
steps.state_change: PlanningAdmissionPending is appended to the episode timeline.
steps.guardrail: Cache absence is reported as unavailable, never interpreted as approval.

paths.name: Recall memory for a user prompt
paths.trigger: UserPromptSubmit with at least 15 characters
paths.cadence: Every substantive user prompt
paths.why: Deliver situated prior experience and relevant playbook pointers before the agent answers or acts.
paths.outcome: Up to six not-yet-seen one-line memory hooks and not-yet-shown skill pointers are injected and attributed.

steps.does: Derive the project from cwd and POST the prompt to /recall with source=hook_user_prompt.
steps.state_change: None locally until results return.
steps.guardrail: Excluded cwd prefixes bypass recall and logging; HTTP timeout is 2.5 seconds.

steps.does: Over-fetch candidates, run the canonical cheap pipeline, drop scaffold node types, apply project boost, and return real knowledge hits.
steps.state_change: When persist=true, a zero-cost Query row and firing rows record what was actually returned.
steps.guardrail: top_k is capped; scaffold nodes remain usable for graph spread but cannot consume delivered slots.

steps.does: Structural resolve, local embedding classification, hybrid lanes, six-signal score, continuity, spread, inhibition, optional engram resolve, token assembly, and telemetry.
steps.state_change: No graph mutation during preparation; process-local caches may load.
steps.guardrail: The canonical ordered stage list includes inhibition and contains no LLM classifier.

steps.does: Convert votes from source lessons and scored skill nodes into pull-based playbook pointers.
steps.state_change: Pointer delivery is logged for later conversion measurement.
steps.guardrail: A skill node is pointer fuel, never a delivered memory hit.

steps.does: Check each hit's (neuron, trigger, tool) pathway against the plasticity suppression projection; withhold suppressed pathways except the deterministic 1-in-k probe slot hashed from (session, pathway).
steps.state_change: Probe deliveries are stamped on the Injection record's `probes` list; suppressed hits land on its `withheld` sibling list — the denominator of the trial of absence, logged even when every hit was withheld.
steps.guardrail: A missing or corrupt projection fails open (deliver); no pathway state may reduce delivery probability to zero, and capsule standing content is never gated here.

steps.does: Dedupe against prior injections/pointers in the episode log and render summaries as background facts, not instructions.
steps.state_change: Injection and SkillPointer JSONL events link delivered neurons to the recall query id; withheld ids stay out of neuron_ids, dedupe, and attribution.
steps.guardrail: Full memory bodies are never ambiently injected; detail stays pull-based.

paths.name: Warn before a risky shell action
paths.trigger: PreToolUse for Bash commands with at least 15 characters
paths.cadence: Before qualifying shell calls
paths.why: Surface high-confidence machine and tool gotchas at the moment they can prevent a repeated failure.
paths.outcome: At most two unseen hits scoring at least 1.12 are injected; no skill pointers interrupt the tool call.

steps.does: Recall on the first 400 command characters with source=hook_pre_tool and project context, then apply the habituation pathway gate keyed per (neuron, PreToolUse, tool).
steps.state_change: Successful delivery is appended to the episode log; suppressed hits are logged withheld, probes stamped — same trial ledger as prompt delivery.
steps.guardrail: Non-Bash tools, short commands, low-score hits, and prior-session duplicates are ignored; the gate fails open.

steps.does: Run the same no-LLM graph path as prompt recall and return scored structured hits.
steps.state_change: Persist query/firing telemetry for later attribution.
steps.guardrail: Provider LLM modules are absent from the recall component.

paths.name: Admit a mapped project mutation
paths.trigger: PreToolUse detects a material operation targeting a mapped project
paths.cadence: Before the first mutation and again after any ledger revision change
paths.why: Keep coding work bound to canonical forward intent without turning memory retrieval into an enforcement mechanism.
paths.outcome: The mutation proceeds only with a current bound admission or an explicit off-ledger reason.

steps.does: Classify the tool and shell command as material/read-only, resolve target paths to the longest matching project ledger, and inspect the session episode.
steps.state_change: None on a permitted read; a denial is returned to the harness before the tool executes.
steps.guardrail: Multi-project mutations are blocked as ambiguous; unknown mutating tools fail toward admission.

steps.does: Validate unfinished record or off-ledger reason and append a PlanningAdmission event pinned to ledger revision/state version.
steps.state_change: Append-only admission receipt in the session episode log.
steps.guardrail: Done, cancelled, or deprioritized records cannot admit bound work.

steps.does: Re-read the latest admission; compare its revision to the local projection before allowing mutation.
steps.state_change: None.
steps.guardrail: Revision drift blocks and requires readmission.

paths.name: Capture session evidence
paths.trigger: PostToolUse and Stop hooks
paths.cadence: After each tool result and at session stop
paths.why: Preserve deeds and outcomes as low-trust evidence for later distillation without storing full file bodies or secrets.
paths.outcome: A per-session JSONL episode becomes distill-ready; planning return is recorded when admitted material work occurred.

steps.does: Summarize allow-listed tool inputs, derive structural success/failure, redact credential-shaped values, and append one event.
steps.state_change: ~/.corvus-mind/episodes/{session_id}.jsonl grows by one line.
steps.guardrail: Excluded cwd prefixes are never logged; arbitrary input fields are dropped; any exception exits zero.

steps.does: On Stop, inspect post-admission successful material tool events and append PlanningReturn with reconcile-required status.
steps.state_change: Execution evidence is returned to the episode timeline; canonical roadmap status does not auto-close.
steps.guardrail: No admission or no material work produces no return receipt.

paths.name: Explicitly recall institutional memory
paths.trigger: Agent calls the corvus-mind recall MCP tool
paths.cadence: On demand
paths.why: Pull full evidence-framed memory when ambient one-line hooks are insufficient.
paths.outcome: Structured hits with content, provenance, timestamps, scores, query id, telemetry, and skill pointers.

steps.does: POST /recall with include_content=true and source=mcp; it imports no application or database modules.
steps.state_change: None in the client.
steps.guardrail: Backend errors are returned as tool JSON instead of crashing the MCP process.

steps.does: Execute cheap hybrid retrieval; in horizontal mode read firing aggregates and bounded spread frontiers from PostgreSQL, checking the shared semantic revision before cosine selection.
steps.state_change: Query/firing telemetry persists by default; committed graph writes become visible to every worker on its next canonical read or semantic revision check.
steps.guardrail: Memory-surface dependency 404s the endpoint on non-memory tenants; database spread caps frontier nodes and returned edges per hop.

paths.name: Save one explicit lesson
paths.trigger: Agent calls remember with claim, evidence, future use, and likely queries
paths.cadence: On demand after verified learning
paths.why: Preserve situated knowledge in a form a future agent can reconstruct without this transcript.
paths.outcome: A novel low-authority lesson is audited and embedded, or a near-duplicate/authoritative write remains queued for review.

steps.does: Send the nine evidence-frame slots to /remember at informational authority.
steps.state_change: None in the client.
steps.guardrail: future_use and likely_queries are required tool arguments.

steps.does: Resolve a scope/project anchor, normalize entities, build the canonical evidence frame, and stage a proposal item.
steps.state_change: Proposal and proposal-item rows describe the candidate before any neuron exists.
steps.guardrail: Missing/malformed frame slots fail with 422; no caller gets an unframed durable memory.

steps.does: Compare nearest active lessons, queue ambiguous duplicates, then classify the proposal by authority, guardrail result, confidence, and region override.
steps.state_change: Proposal stays proposed or becomes approved/applied by the system gate.
steps.guardrail: The memory tenant requires approval for dedup; writes above guidance cannot auto-commit.

steps.does: Apply the approved proposal through typed, validated, audited handlers inside a savepoint.
steps.state_change: Neuron/refinement/action rows change atomically within the outer transaction.
steps.guardrail: Handler failure rolls back its savepoint and records a failed Action rather than a partial success.

steps.does: Embed a newly created neuron, wire nearest-neighbor edges, and update the writer's optional local projections before commit returns.
steps.state_change: PostgreSQL becomes canonical at commit; embedding/active-set triggers advance the shared semantic revision so every worker reloads before its next semantic use.
steps.guardrail: Cache/index update occurs only after a real created neuron id exists; local updates are optimizations, not cross-worker coherence.

paths.name: Distill episodes into candidate lessons
paths.trigger: corvus-mind-distill.timer POSTs /distill/run
paths.cadence: Timer opportunity every 30 minutes; only quiescent undistilled logs run, max five sessions by default
paths.why: Convert noisy tool evidence and user corrections into durable, future-useful lessons while preventing self-reinforcement and agent-assertion pollution.
paths.outcome: Gate-passed candidates traverse the same lesson write path; attribution rewards/penalizes previously injected memories; recurrence nominations for withheld lessons pass a deterministic admission gate; successful logs receive markers.

steps.does: Offer a bounded POST to /distill/run.
steps.state_change: Starts one batch request.
steps.guardrail: Service timeout and per-run session cap bound work.

steps.does: Load redacted events, injections, user messages, and lowest-trust assistant assertions; request the opus capability grade for framed candidates and attribution verdicts (Codex Sol primary by default, Anthropic Opus fallback).
steps.state_change: Provider usage is recorded; no candidate is saved yet.
steps.guardrail: Assistant-origin candidates require a cited corroborating tool event; instruction-shaped and already-injected lessons are dropped.

steps.does: Route each surviving candidate through proposal, near-duplicate, authority, and Action Bus controls.
steps.state_change: Candidate becomes a neuron or remains a review proposal.
steps.guardrail: One bad candidate is counted and skipped without aborting the session batch.

steps.does: Reward load-bearing injections, demote contradicted ones, leave unused unchanged, and attach SynapticLearningEvent when query-linked.
steps.state_change: avg_utility and attribution telemetry move from observed session outcomes.
steps.guardrail: One verdict per label per session; ambiguous delivery channel is labeled rather than guessed.

steps.does: Present lessons a delivery trial withheld from this session and ask whether each one's documented failure actually recurred in the log.
steps.state_change: None — nominations are model output, not decisions; refused ones are counted and dropped.
steps.guardrail: Only lessons never delivered anywhere in the session qualify; delivered-and-failed is contradiction evidence for the attribution lane, not trial harm.

steps.does: Admit a nomination only when its cited event token-matches both the actual episode events and the withheld lesson's own failure text, then log recurrence.verified per withheld pathway.
steps.state_change: Ground-truth false-kill evidence lands in the actions log for the plasticity fold to consume.
steps.guardrail: Uncited or unrelated nominations are refused (deeds-corroborated pattern); a missed match leaves the trial running with the pathway's floor intact — the safe failure direction.

steps.does: Commit and write a .distilled marker only after the session completes successfully.
steps.state_change: The log leaves the ready queue; failures without markers retry later.
steps.guardrail: Per-log failure does not stop other ready logs.

paths.name: Compile lessons into playbooks and standing policy
paths.trigger: corvus-mind-compile.timer POSTs /compile/run
paths.cadence: Daily opportunity; bounded new skills per run
paths.why: Convert related trusted memories into reusable procedures while keeping graph truth, projections, and harness delivery synchronized.
paths.outcome: Stale projections retire to archive; eligible clusters produce mind-* skills and graph-shadow nodes; charter is deterministically rebuilt.

steps.does: Load eligible lessons, build same-scope embedding components, split oversized clusters, and reconcile manifest entries against disk/source health.
steps.state_change: None until stale or new artifacts are identified.
steps.guardrail: Source utility, active/superseded state, cluster growth, size caps, and namespacing constrain eligibility.

steps.does: Request the opus capability grade to compose one focused name, description, and Markdown playbook from each new eligible cluster; default routing selects Codex Sol with Anthropic Opus fallback.
steps.state_change: Model usage is added to the compile report.
steps.guardrail: Invalid JSON, non-mind-* names, or missing fields emit no skill.

steps.does: Write generated SKILL.md with source-neuron provenance and project it to supported harnesses.
steps.state_change: Canonical and harness skill files plus compiled-skills manifest change.
steps.guardrail: Only namespaced generated directories are written; retired renderings are archived, not deleted.

steps.does: Create an informational skill-shadow neuron and evidence-link edges from its source lessons.
steps.state_change: The graph can score the skill as pointer fuel and visualize its source cluster.
steps.guardrail: Recall filters skill nodes from memory hits.
